title: Edge node catalog reconcile & health scoring (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic set of notes for the node catalog reconciliation loop and a unified health scoring model that the control plane can use for routing/policy decisions across regions. Focus is on: (1) a label schema that surfaces GPU capability tiers, (2) a lightweight health score composed from telemetry and state signals, and (3) reconciliation semantics for multi-region and transient-network cases.

Background / Why this matters:
- Routing and autoscaling decisions depend on up-to-date, comparable node profiles (capability + health).
- We have many regional fleets with different GPU types and noisy telemetry; need a single canonical view per logical node (or node-group) that can be reliably consumed by the smart router.
- Existing inventory docs cover catalogs and node fingerprints; this doc focuses on the reconciliation operator + scoring algorithm that turns raw telemetry into a routing-safe abstraction.

Goals:
- Minimal eventual consistency: nodes show up within a bounded staleness window (defaults: 30s heartbeats, 120s TTL).
- Deterministic conflict resolution across regions (no split-brain for labels that affect routing).
- Health score in [0..100] that is monotonic with respect to observed risk and easy to explain to SREs/product owners.
- Expose enough label granularity to support model-to-GPU mapping (e.g., quantized 8-bit friendly vs full fp16).

Labels (recommended canonical keys):
- redwood/node/id -> stable id (UUID from agent)
- redwood/node/region -> region string (e.g., us-west1)
- redwood/node/zone -> optional zone
- redwood/node/role -> inference|batch|infra|gpu-cache
- redwood/gpu/family -> a100|h100|rtx6000|v100 (normalized token)
- redwood/gpu/compute_tier -> high|medium|low  # abstracted compute capability for routing rules
- redwood/gpu/memory_gb -> integer (rounded)
- redwood/gpu/mps_enabled -> true|false
- redwood/node/maintenance -> draining|offline|available
- redwood/node/last_upgrade -> ISO8601 timestamp (agent-set)
- redwood/node/labels_provenance -> agent|manager|manual (used for conflict resolution)

Notes on labels: keep keys namespaced, keep values small and enumerable. Avoid freeform strings for compute_tier and family so matching policies stay simple.

Reconciliation loop (operator) sketch:
1) Agent heartbeat: every 30s send small payload: node_id, labels (as above), small telemetry delta (GPU temp, mem_util_pct, queue_latency_50pct), monotonic counters for error events, node_version.
2) Local aggregator in region writes to regional catalog with event timestamp and sequence number.
3) Cross-region sync: region-level digest (node_id + seq + timestamp + hash(labels+meta)) is gossiped every 10s to a global control plane endpoint.
4) Conflict resolution: pick record with the highest (timestamp, sequence) tuple where timestamp is server-received time and sequence is agent monotonic. If timestamps within 5s and sequences mismatch, prefer labels_provenance priority: manager > agent > manual.
5) TTL: if no heartbeats for TTL (default 120s), node state becomes STALE. Stale nodes are excluded by default from routing; a policy flag allow-stale-for-eviction exists for emergency failover.

Why sequence + timestamp: Helps with short reorders and avoids relying solely on wall-clock across regions. Sequence provides local monotonic order; timestamp breaks ties for nodes behind NATs or with delayed forwarding.

Health signals (raw signals we store):
- gpu_temp_c (per-GPU, recent max)
- gpu_mem_used_pct (per-GPU 90p)
- gpu_util_pct (recent mean, 1m)
- cuda_driver_mismatch (bool)
- ecc_errors_last_hour (count)
- nvlink_errors_last_hour (count)
- queue_latency_p50ms (ms)
- infra_disk_pressure (bool)
- network_rt_ms (p50/p95)
- recent_restarts (count, last 24h)
- system_load_1m (host-level)

Health score model (proposal):
- score starts at 100
- subtract weighted penalties for signals exceeding thresholds. All penalties clipped to 0..100.
- example weights/thresholds (configurable per fleet):
  - gpu_temp_c: if max_temp > 85C -> penalty = min(30, (max_temp - 85) * 1.5)
  - gpu_mem_used_pct: if > 95% -> penalty = 25; else if > 85% -> penalty = 10
  - gpu_util_pct: if < 5% and recent_restarts > 0 -> penalty = 20 (instability signature)
  - cuda_driver_mismatch: penalty = 40 (hard)
  - ecc_errors_last_hour: penalty = min(30, ecc_errors * 5)
  - queue_latency_p50ms: penalty = min(25, (p50 / 50))  # 50ms baseline
  - network_rt_p95: penalty = min(20, (p95 - 30) / 5)
  - recent_restarts: penalty += min(20, recent_restarts * 5)
- health_score = max(0, 100 - sum(penalties))
- bucket tags exposed: health_category: healthy|degraded|critical (>=80, 50-79, <50)

Rationale: Keep formula additive and explainable. Operators can change weights per cluster or GPU family. Keep heavy penalties for driver/firmware issues so we can quarantine nodes quickly.

Health provenance & auditability:
- always store the contributing signals and the penalty breakdown for the last 6 hours (time-series-minimum footprint). This helps debug why router avoided a node.
- expose an audit link in console to the raw telemetry stream and the reconciliation events for a node_id.

Integration with routing / model placement:
- Router queries node catalog with filters: region, compute_tier >= X, health_category != critical, maintenance != draining. Also supports custom policy functions (e.g., prefer nodes with mps_enabled for concurrency).
- When capacity is constrained, router can fallback to lower tier models or queued request fallback. Use the health_score to prefer stable nodes for long-running generation.
- Support for variant mapping: catalog holds model compatibility hints (e.g., model_v1.quant_8bit -> allowed compute_tiers [high,medium]) supplied by model-onboarding pipeline.

Multi-region considerations / partition tolerance:
- Gossiped digests avoid shipping full telemetry across regions frequently. Full telemetry fetched on demand when router evaluates a candidate node.
- Conflict windows: if regions are partitioned for > TTL, each region can mark nodes as regionally-local-canonical; a reconciliation policy later merges by sequence/timestamp.
- For large fleets, shard the catalog by node_id hash to reduce cross-region join work. Shards assigned to region-leaders; failover if leader unreachable.

Operational playbook (short):
- OnNodeFlap: if a node oscillates between healthy/degraded three times in 30m, mark for manual inspection, create ticket PLAT-4216.
- DriverMismatchAlert: auto-quarantine node (mark maintenance=draining) and trigger AMI/agent upgrade job.
- StaleNodesSweep: nightly job that removes records older than 30d and moves them to cold storage.

Telemetry volume and retention note:
- Heartbeat payloads are tiny (approx 1KB). Full per-GPU telemetry sampled at 1m -> expect ~200KB/node/day. Default retention: 6d for raw telemetry, 90d for aggregated rollups.

Security & privacy:
- Agent signs heartbeats with node key; control plane verifies signatures before accepting label updates (prevents spoofed capability claims).
- Personally identifying fields: none in catalog. Hostnames are sanitized.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we prefer vector-clock style resolution instead of (timestamp, seq)? Pros/cons: vector clocks are accurate but heavier to exchange.
- Policy to automatically relax health thresholds during region-wide incidents (e.g., cross-region network partitions) — should we autoscale to accept lower scores temporarily?
- How to represent GPU-microarchitecture details in a compact way that still helps kernel selection? (e.g., sm_count, arch_rev)
- Backfill job: when we change compute_tier classification heuristics, who backfills the catalog? operator or ephemeral job?

Quick checklist for implementation sprint:
- [ ] Agent: add labels_provenance + monotonic seq to heartbeat
- [ ] Regional aggregator: compute region digest and gossiper
- [ ] Global reconciler: implement (timestamp, seq) resolution + TTL semantics
- [ ] Health scoring service: implement rule config + penalty breakdown storage
- [ ] Router integration: query API and fallbacks for compute_tier mapping

References and related docs:
- existing inventory service spec: /platform-engineering/inventory-service-discovery-health-probes (see related files in drive)
- model onboarding mapping table: confluence.redwood/internal/Models/compatibility
- linear ticket: PLAT-4216 (node flap follow-up)

Notes to self: Keep the first iteration conservative (strict TTLs, high penalties for driver/firmware). Make scoring config-driven per-fleet so we can iterate without node restarts.

-- End of notes --
